title: Machine-learning-guided BioTAK biomarker score separates Takotsubo from coronary syndrome
summary: In 3615 patients with acute coronary syndrome or Takotsubo syndrome, machine-learning-guided feature selection and logistic regression produced a five-item biomarker score (NT-proBNP, peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase, soluble LOX-1, LDL cholesterol, and sex). Its AUC was 0.97 (95% CI 0.95-0.98) in the development cohort of 1823 patients (69 Takotsubo) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.90-0.96) in an independent cohort of 1792 (77 Takotsubo). Using predefined thresholds the score stratified almost 90% of patients before angiography. Machine learning only selected features, and Takotsubo cases are few.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided feature selection combined with logistic regression
organization: National Health Service; University of Leicester; University of Zurich

evidence.tested: External validation in an independent cohort of 1792 patients.
evidence.unknown: Prospective impact on diagnostic pathways; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selected the biomarker features for the logistic-regression score.
